# Startup readback: AI-20

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Make the canonical runtime enforce the product’s recurring $5 target / $10 hard cap and separate per-run on-demand cap before any paid Responses request. Keep deterministic cost arithmetic, usage accounting, forecast inputs and reporting traceable end to end.

1. A call cannot reach OpenAI unless an effective, provenance-backed price exists and an atomic reservation succeeds under the correct recurring or on-demand cap, including concurrent reservations and retries.
2. Provider input/cached/output/reasoning/search usage is reconciled to exact USD actual cost through the canonical result/settlement path; cancellation/failure releases unused reservations; retries and duplicate completion do not double-charge; provider-reported variance is persisted and explainable.
3. Monthly forecasts and Spend UI distinguish actual vs expected completed cost, remaining recurring estimates, recurring/on-demand/combined totals, reserved amount and confidence/provenance without changing historical prices.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

- AI-15 (Done): canonical run/queue lifecycle, idempotent provider request IDs and atomic report/usage commit; prior live proof is one bounded gpt-5.6-luna Responses call, zero search, $0.00117, $0.05 cap, with trace/reconciled cost. Keep cost reservation inside this path; direct/internal function calls are not equivalent.
- AI-16 (Done): evaluated/promoted prompt/model governance and versioned pricing provenance. Preserve permitted model/cap pairs and exact approved model routing.
- AI-19 (Done): correlation/trace/audit evidence and safe diagnostics. Use authorized evidence APIs; do not add direct reads of protected trace tables.
- Build Spec §§11.3, 14.1–14.5, 16.2: versioned effective prices; worst-reasonable pre-call reserve; atomic hard caps; separate on-demand ceiling; deterministic forecast formula/confidence; never rewrite historical costs.
- Agent Spec §§1.1 and 10.2 plus SYS-004/SYS-006: deterministic software owns arithmetic and reservation; Systems owns cost controls; hard-cap rejection and AI-call cost tracing are explicit capability invariants.
- Frontend Constitution §16.2: Spend page must show cost/forecast evidence with clear hierarchy.
- Using existing ai-execute → reserve_instrumented_ai_call → OpenAI Responses webhook → canonical commit/settlement → protected trace/forecast reads; integration risks: DB-03/DB-05/DB-09/DB-12, AI-01/AI-02, DB-02, OPS-01, ACC-01.

## Implementation and boundaries

Inspect and extend the existing pricing, budget/reservation, webhook usage parsing/settlement, forecast RPC/UI and producer-consumer paths. Any migration is forward-only, gets a fresh prefix after checking main and sibling PRs, and keeps RLS/ACLs plus exact pricing history intact. All HTTP/provider output is schema validated; unknown/stale pricing, provider usage gaps, over-cap actuals, DB errors and retries fail closed or remain visibly reconcilable. No hard-cap increases, direct privileged table grants, unbounded real calls or alternate execution path.

## Local tests and commands

Profile: cost-runtime. First reproduce the narrowest violated invariant; add deterministic tests for reservation races/cap boundaries, stale/unknown prices, estimate precision/allowances, cancellation/failure release, idempotent retries/duplicate webhooks, usage variants, over-reservation variance and forecast inputs/confidence. Add pgTAP/RLS/ACL and caller tests for changed DB boundaries; cover relevant API/UI state. Then run corepack pnpm verify:changed on the final ticket head and required CI; do not repeat identical proof layers unnecessarily.

## Hosted proof and readiness

Exactly one bounded real staging Responses call through the canonical orchestrator, using the lowest-cost permitted model, no search/actions, and an accepted cap. Verify exact candidate SHA/tree, reservation before provider call, provider-reported usage, calculated actual cost, settled/released reservation, correlated trace and no cap discrepancy. Provider-call/setup state must be validated without exposing secrets. Reuse the existing headed acceptance producer/validator/consumer and staging lease (ACC-01); pause for the operator at any visible-browser sign-in/MFA gate (ACC-02). After merge, require the pipeline’s bounded production smoke.

## Delegation and blockers

AI-20 is owned by root in the isolated `ai-20-cost` worktree through merge; no subagents modify this ticket. The required hosted gate is one bounded real staging Responses call after exact-head CI. Operator sign-in/MFA remains manual if the headed browser prompts. No code or credential blocker is active. AI-27 currently owns the local Supabase lease, and AI-35's duplicate-sync proof is waiting for operator sign-in; keep DB and staging leases serialized.
